articles.headline: Why Goldman Is Cautious on Micron Stock Ahead of Earnings
articles.text:
Why Goldman Is Cautious on Micron Stock Ahead of Earnings
Micron Technology shares were edging down early on Friday to end a volatile week for the memory-chip company. Analysts at Goldman Sachs are wary of the stock ahead of its earnings report later this month.

articles.headline: Micron's stock rebounds after 'healthy' reset, and analysts see blue skies ahead
articles.text:
Tech Stocks
Micron’s stock rebounds after ‘healthy’ reset, and analysts see blue skies ahead
Micron shares trade cheaply relative to S&P 500 peers, but two analysts point to ways the valuation multiple can expand
Memory stocks are back on the upswing, and Morgan Stanley analysts say their recent breather was necessary to support more explosive gains.
While Micron’s stock rose 11.7% on Thursday, it’s off nearly 10% from its peak close on June 3. Shares of South Korea-listed memory-chip makers Samsung Electronics KR:005930 and SK Hynix KR:000660 are down 18% and 13%, respectively, from their recent closing highs.

articles.headline: Micron, Intel drag the tech sector into a new bearish phase. Will the correction last this time?
articles.text:
Tech Stocks
Micron, Marvell drag the tech sector into a new bearish phase. Will the correction last this time?
The SPDR tech-sector ETF officially entered a correction — the previous one lasted five months, and ended less than two months ago
The selloff in the tech sector that has heightened investor anxiety over the past week graduated to a new phase on Wednesday: The pullback is over, and it’s now officially a correction.
If recent history is any guide, that would seem to dash hopes for a quick recovery. But there’s also reason for investors not to worry about a lower-for-longer scenario, given that what’s fueling the weakness is more technical in nature than fundamental.

What's at Stake for the Market
Venture capitalist Marc Andreessen famously said that software was eating the world. Now, AI is eating the stock market.
That is why the SpaceX IPO isn't just a big deal for Elon Musk; it's a big deal for just about every investor, whether they realize it or not.
SpaceX, by virtue of its February merger with xAI, is the first of the money-losing frontier artificial intelligence companies to go public, beating OpenAI and Anthropic, albeit with a twist. (SpaceX is also a rocket company with a profitable, fast-growing communications business, Starlink.)
